author: DMGuide
title: Played one, played ’em all
content:
Mechanically identical to half the other merge games on the app store; I assume it’s quietly the same parent company slapping a new theme and different art on the same codebase, then spinning up a new shell company to release it.

The story starts fine but quickly drops in quality as soon as you’re past the first arc. Though presented as a mystery, there’s no real way to figure out the culprit of each arc; clues are brought up and discarded on a whim. The characters are indistinguishable from each other, all speaking in the same voice and using the same bizarrely outdated slang. 

And of course, like all the others, this game is trying as hard as it can to squeeze you for money, with rewards in events always *just* out of reach unless you crack open your wallet.

author: Ggm*1968
title: The Energy System Kills the Fun
content:
I’ve played Mystery Town long enough to reach level 113, so I feel like I’ve given the game a fair chance.
The game itself is fun, but the energy system completely ruins the experience. You’re constantly interrupted by pop-ups trying to get you to buy more energy. The game doesn’t give enough opportunities to earn energy for free like other games do.
When your energy finally refreshes after waiting hours, you only get 100 energy, which isn’t even enough to complete a single task. You can spend gems on more energy, but those disappear just as quickly.
The card collection system is also disappointing. After reaching level 113, it still feels almost useless because it takes forever to earn anything worthwhile from it.
What’s most frustrating is that I’ve earned over 1.2 million coins, yet they can’t be used to buy energy or gems. They’re only useful for building things, and even then you can’t build whenever you want—you have to complete specific tasks first. Building is also one of the few ways to earn extra energy, so your progress constantly feels restricted. It’s really starting to feel discouraging to play anymore

author: Rosie T. Clown
title: The Best Merge Game For One Main Reason
content:
TLDR; This merge game actually lets you play it instead of waiting around for things to recharge. 

I originally found this game on KashKick and downloaded it to earn a little bit of money on the side like I’ve done for 50+ other games. Out of all merge games, this one has to be the BEST one by far. In other merge games, the things you have to click on to produce items (ex. the Shaker produces bottles of beer, the Oven produces gingerbread cookies) usually have a certain amount of clicks before it “runs out of energy” or something like that and you have to wait an unnecessary amount of time before it recharges. With this one, the main items don’t seem to have that unnecessary “recharge” and the ones that do (shaker, display case) only take tops 3 minutes to recharge. It shows they really do want you to play their game for as long as possible! A lot of merge games I play make you wait 2+ hours to recharge an item after getting it to produce just 10 items, it’s crazy! By the time I’m done completing an order the item recharging is done and I can continue clicking on it to produce what I need. So that alone makes me love this game, but it doesn’t end there! The amount of gems you need to spend to earn extra things (ex. more energy, unlocking a bubble holding an extra item) is more than fair, if not a little cheaper than expected! But then again, I’m just used to merge games trying to grab your cash more than just trying to keep your attention towards the game itself. You don’t have to pay to win in this game! It’s purely based off how hard you work at it. Yeah you can buy extra gems or energy, but the game doesn’t make it a necessity to play it more and that’s better than most merge games out there. Also, there are always challenges to play, so not only does that allow you to gain more energy (and other awesome items), but it also gives you a variety of things to play around with. That’s pretty darn cool in my book! The storyline and completing orders to build stuff and level up is a sweet cherry on top. 
Please don’t change this game, this is genuinely the best merge game I’ve ever played just for the mere fact you actually allow us to play the game for as long as we wish. Genuinely better than Merge Dragons which I’ve played for about 5 years in my younger years as I thought that was the best merge game.

author: Banshe1211
title: If only the game allowed the player to play
content:
The game treats the player like they are cannot think for themselves. Not even a tenth of a second goes by before the game is flashing what to do next. There is zero time to decide your next move. 

It is bad enough when games do not allow you to skip the tutorial, this one the tutorial never stops. The games all copy each other. Most people don’t need a tutorial. This isn’t even good for children. The only benefit of screen time is cognitive exercise this game doesn’t give them enough time to think about the next step it just instantly points it out. This teaches instant gratification and let the device think for you.
The game has potential if it would only treat the player with respect and assume intelligence instead of stupidity of the player.

author: syr_kyr
title: I like this game but WARNING: Multi device sync is buggy and you’ll lose progress
content:
I enjoy this game even though I think they’re stingy on energy.

That aside, I’m upset this evening as I came back to my game I had been working on during my breaks all day and found the progress was reset to the beginning of the day. Everything I accomplished and earned over the course of the day is now gone. Due to the nature of the times events I can’t just quickly get it back. 

I think this happened because it synced to the OLDER of two device saves. Why would it do that? It doesn’t even ask you, it just seems to “pick one”.

This is a severe bug that needs to be addressed if you’re gonna offer multiple device support. This game has been a bit of solace for me in a hard time and it sounds stupid but im honestly devastated that this happened.
